An optional descent into Abismo Anhumas cave can be arranged around 20 km west of Bonito. Beyond a narrow opening lies an enormous underground chamber. The descent on a rope system takes you approximately 72 m down.

At the bottom is a clear underground lake with large stalactites. Snorkelling and diving take place among submerged limestone formations. Visits are limited to small numbers of groups, preserving the quiet and the feeling of being in a secluded underground space.

These statues face the ocean, an uncommon orientation on the island. According to local tradition, they are associated with the first seafarers to arrive on Rapa Nui. The central part of the island has fewer large beaches and more open grasslands, so the row of seven figures stands out particularly clearly against the sky and ocean.

The journey then continues to Puna Pau. Red tuff was quarried here for the cylindrical headdresses of the moai. Its reddish colour differs noticeably from the main volcanic stone used for the statues, so even the quarry itself helps explain how the separate elements of the monuments were made.

The viewpoint offers views of Hanga Roa and the coastal bays.

The excursion lasts approximately four hours.

Laguna Colorada, or the Red Lagoon, in Eduardo Avaroa National Park is a particular highlight. Depending on the light and temperature, its waters take on shades ranging from bright red to deep burgundy. Numerous flamingos live here, while llamas, chinchillas and other Andean wildlife can be found in the surrounding area.

Along the way, you will stop at the Sol de Mañana geysers and the thermal springs by Lake Chalviri. After the excursion, transfer to the Bolivia–Chile border, complete the border formalities and change vehicles. The journey then continues with a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama, Chile.

The boat travels along Amazonian waterways beside tropical forested banks. During the trip, you can try fishing for piranhas with a rod directly from the boat.

The next stop is dedicated to the lives of caboclos, local residents of the Amazon. You will learn about their daily activities, traditions and customs before setting off on a walk through the jungle.

Your guide will introduce the forest's plants and animals, explain how to distinguish edible plants from poisonous ones, and demonstrate jungle survival techniques. The programme also includes an introduction to traditional shooting with poison-tipped arrows under the guide's supervision.

Another part of the trip focuses on pink river dolphins. The programme includes an introduction to the animals and opportunities to swim near them, feed them and take photographs. The exact form of interaction is confirmed when booking, taking into account current rules and conditions on site.

This is a combined excursion programme departing from an Amazon lodge with an English-speaking guide. The timing of individual stops and the order of visits are agreed for the trip.

Amboró is a day amid Bolivia's cloud forest, with tall ferns, lush vegetation, birds and nature trails. After the forest portion of the route, the excursion continues to Cuevas waterfalls.

The park visit includes a walk along its trails. The main attraction here is the cloud forest itself: its plants, birdsong and opportunities to observe local wildlife.

The journey back to Santa Cruz begins in the afternoon, with a stop at Cuevas waterfalls. Here you can relax beside the water and spend time among lush vegetation.
